7	### THE CENTRAL STORY: Ostrey Hollow milk-testing station and the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association
8	
9	#### Geography / entities
10	- **Larrow Valley** — the valley; contains **Larrow Green** (site of the main creamery, on Larrow Creek, built 1891) and, seven miles up-valley, **Ostrey Hollow**, at the head of which stood the **skimming station**.
11	- **Hessel Bottom** — a wet meadow below the Ostrey Hollow hamlet; the best milk in the Hollow came from here. Seven farms had grazing/haying rights on Hessel Bottom; the largest was **Emmet Brant's**.
12	- **Ashlin** — the county seat/town where hearings, the Association's office (later), the historical society, and legal business took place.
13	- **Farland** — site of a college with a library (where Ivy Keddie later worked/taught, and where Merle Strawn's notebooks were held).
14	- **Redlow Ridge**, **Vessey County** — location of the **Alder Corners Cheese Company** (a rival/comparison creamery, used for cross-checking milk tests).
15	- **Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association** — organized 1889 by valley farmers at Larrow Green. By-laws drafted by **Gideon Vose**, who was elected first president in 1889 and served until 1911 (22 years — longest of any president). Gideon Vose died in 1917.
16	- **Article VII** of the by-laws (adopted 1892, the year after the creamery opened), quoted in full by Effie Loomis (r02): *"Every patron shall be paid for the milk he delivers according to the number of pounds of butter fat contained in it, ascertained by test, and not according to the weight of the milk; and the test of the station where he delivers shall govern."* Key point emphasized by Loomis: "the test of the station where he delivers shall govern" — no appeal from the station's own test. This clause is called "the hinge of the whole Ostrey Hollow business."
